inventory.overview: The study combines a classical GPU text experiment on DBpedia14 title-plus-content classification with a separate synthetic quantum-circuit schedule experiment. All 94 registered main runs and eight common text warmups completed. Classical confirmation includes 15 endpoints and quantum confirmation includes 40 endpoints.
inventory.findings: Hash18 text macro-F1 was 97.659%, compared with 97.642% for current content routing and 97.602% for shared adapters. The primary mean gain was 0.01694 percentage points and its paired 95% interval crossed zero. In the quantum task, untied assigned circuits reached 81.44%, the original schedule 71.83%, fixed depth four 93.32%, and the matched-information MLP129 99.04%.
inventory.limitations: The text result does not establish a resolved primary improvement. Changing circuit scheduling improved the selected quantum comparison but the fixed-depth and classical controls performed better. This is local simulation, without quantum advantage or physical hardware evidence. Historical path bindings and exact NumPy replay guards limit relocation. The two task families must not be conflated.

inventory.overview: All 104 registered training runs completed: 39 development and 65 confirmation. Thirteen methods continued to five-seed confirmation on fresh synthetic circle data. Independent replay checked 65 endpoints, 104000 predictions and 150 saved shot arrays.
inventory.findings: Confirmation mean macro-F1 was 97.42% for k-means routed depth-two circuits, 90.10% for hash routing with the same 40 circuit angles, 94.06% for a fixed depth-four circuit and 98.70% for the larger classical MLP. Routing improved the circuit model, while the spatial partition also added classical capacity.
inventory.limitations: One synthetic task and five confirmation training seeds do not establish quantum advantage or real-domain generalization. A development numerical-threshold failure and a verification-only pre-confirmation amendment are preserved in the historical evidence. Confirmation had zero ambiguous predictions. Local Aer checks used 150 circuits and 3840000 simulated measurement shots; separate probability-level binomial analysis is not hardware execution or device-noise simulation.

inventory.overview: Nine combinations of model family and routing were evaluated: two-qubit depth-two circuits, raw-input ReLU MLPs and 25-feature trigonometric logit models, each with global, coordinate-hash or train-only k-means routing. All 54 development and 135 confirmation endpoints completed 200 rounds and 15000 optimizer updates. Confirmation covered two independent circle populations and a rotated ellipse.
inventory.findings: Q2 k-means mean macro-F1 was 98.32%, 97.16% and 94.41% across the three confirmation populations. Spatial routing substantially improved Q2 relative to hash routing, but trigonometric k-means models had lower BCE throughout. Global MLP and trigonometric controls also outperformed Q2 k-means in mean F1 and BCE. Q2 versus the small routed MLP was unresolved across training seeds.
inventory.limitations: Five seeds, synthetic tasks, fixed routers and unequal capacities do not isolate a circuit-specific benefit or establish quantum advantage, equivalence, speed or real-world generalization. Seed intervals and conditional record bootstraps answer different questions. Local readiness covered 45 quantum checkpoints, 1440 validation fixture circuits and 720 measured Aer experiments totaling 737280 simulated shots; 199065600 represented binomial trials are separate. Illustrative noise is not device calibration.

inventory.findings: Eleven small model recipes compare flexible circuit readouts with neural-network and trigonometric controls on fresh two-dimensional circle and ellipse tasks. Learned scalar and five-moment readouts improve on the legacy output, while strong trigonometric controls retain the most attractive accuracy and cost combination. The random frozen circuit core performs substantially worse. The study completed 66 development and 165 confirmation endpoints, in addition to 22 engineering endpoints.
inventory.limitations: The results concern small two-dimensional synthetic classifiers on classical CPU hardware. Five paired seeds and one split per family do not establish population-wide or real-world generalization. Historical prior-version scores are context, not paired evidence of improvement. Local compilation, noise and shot results are simulator evidence, with no physical-QPU result or quantum-advantage claim. The full proposed language architecture was not benchmarked.

The richer readout improves the difficult clean-boundary tasks; the routed trigonometric control remains stronger there. Exact classical coefficient conversion accelerates the same trained circuits without changing their decisions; it is not another efficacy arm. The study completed 48 development and 120 confirmation endpoints, plus 24 engineering endpoints.

inventory.findings: Geometric routing consistently outperformed matched-count hash routing. The global Trig121 control led the two harder clean tasks (98.47% checkerboard and 96.57% spiral macro-F1 versus 76.57% and 86.82% for the flexible circuit). Classical compilation preserved checked class predictions and accelerated single-input circuit calls 4.28–4.58 times. These historical measurements do not establish quantum advantage.
inventory.models_tasks: Eight arms compare scalar and flexible routed two-qubit circuit emulation, geometric and matched-count hash routing, routed/global trigonometric controls and an MLP on checkerboard, spiral, noisy annulus and rare disks. Confirmation uses eight independent populations per task and two paired optimizer seeds per population.
inventory.limits: 608 registered fits, including 512 confirmation endpoints; 20 primary paired population-level BCE contrasts. Small-sample interval assumptions, four synthetic families and host-specific timing limit generalization. Finite-shot sensitivity was historical local simulation, not physical hardware.

inventory.findings: Priority improved four of eight direct registered BCE comparisons, with the other four inconclusive; none established more than 0.01 BCE improvement across the entire interval. Priority did not close the routed circuit gap to the wider global baseline on checkerboard or spiral. Exact conversion preserved predictions (maximum probability difference below 2.62e-14) and improved local latency.
inventory.models_tasks: Ten arms pair uniform and priority sampling with MultiK, MultiHash, TrigK, TrigHash and TrigG121 on fresh checkerboard, spiral, noisy annulus and rare-disk populations. Confirmation uses eight independent populations per task with two paired optimizer seeds.
inventory.limits: 40 engineering, 80 development and 640 confirmation fits, plus four preselected clean retrains. All 20 primary comparisons are retained. Reproduction fits are not new independent populations. Three timing sessions varied; retained source reports preserve these limits. No physical quantum or new finite-shot campaign is claimed.

inventory.findings: Learned circuit routing won five, lost three and was inconclusive in four of twelve primary BCE contrasts; three wins exceeded the 0.01 practical reference throughout their adjusted intervals. G121 remained much better on checkerboard and spiral. MLP4 led the descriptive Banknote check. Exact conversion preserved 276 circuit predictors and 1,380 expert cores.
inventory.models_tasks: Plan B compares hard geometric routing, fixed soft mixtures, learned soft mixtures, parameter-count-matched residual controls and G121. Four synthetic families use eight confirmation populations and two paired optimizer seeds. Banknote Authentication is a secondary fixed grouped split with five optimizer seeds and additional MLP2, MLP4 and LR2 controls.
inventory.limits: 48 engineering, 72 development, 636 confirmation and four clean retraining fits. Banknote is one fixed split, not five independent datasets. Shared diagnostic numerical primitives, small-sample t assumptions, mixture costs, local timing and absent physical hardware constrain claims. The original top-level READ_ME.txt is a stale preparation notice; final report and acceptance records govern completion.
